decisions.reason: Despite weaker recent visibility, its flagship status and close fit with the firm's sustainability-led reusable-packaging strategy justify continued support unless performance is clearly below aspiration.
The foldable large container line sits squarely in the firm's core transport-packaging business, so a large firm with slack would normally keep it absent strong evidence of underperformance.
Although it has not remained prominent, the stackable crate line still matches core customer needs and is likely to be retained while results remain uncertain rather than clearly unsatisfactory.
After several years without visible momentum, this pallet line looks like an overlapping variant whose returns may be falling below aspiration, making redeployment of resources more attractive.

This pallet variant appears easier to substitute within the broader pallet offering, and continued low salience suggests it is a reasonable candidate for pruning if its results lag internal and peer benchmarks.
